details.detail: Wing planform, sweep and raked tip seen from 13A-30A, and in studio plan and front views. It matches the ACAP digitisation, and the raked tip reads correctly in the plan view. Lit upper-wing tone in q12/f_19A is #9ba2ab, against #9ca1a5 in the F-GSQR_1 cabin photo.

In-flight wing shape. The model uses a straight linear-dihedral crest, so from 17A/19A the leading edge and far edge are straight lines. In both F-GSQR cruise photos the outer wing and raked tip curve visibly upward (1 g bending).

Black main-gear alignment stripe (tail-camera reference, chordwise at the outer main-wheel line) is missing. The ANA yellow ice-detection spot on it is also missing. Both photos from this seat zone show the stripe as the most prominent marking on the wing.
Slat, spoiler, flaperon, flap and aileron seams. Thin dark matte strips lifted 12 mm, with no shimmer seen in the renders. Their width and contrast are close to the F-GSQR seams.

Flap-track fairings (canoes). Their positions and the length they overhang the trailing edge are plausible. The aft half tapers to a thin spike with a small nub (35 % depth floor), where the real fairings stay deep and slab-sided with a blunt rounded end.
GE90-115B nacelle: white fan cowl with no titles, silver lip, dark fan face and cowl split lines. Proportions and colour match ANA JA796A/JA797A from 11A/13A.

Pylon. From 13A it reads as a flat plank 16 cm tall along the cowl crest, rendered #3e4b62 (dark blue) next to the #c9d2dc cowl. On ANA the pylon and strut are light grey, the same tone as the wing (JA797A).

Day sky at the window (winExp 1). The top of the pane is #abc2d8 and the horizon #d3d9dd: pale grey-blue. Cruise photos at the same elevations show #4d7098-#6789ae (F-GSQR_1) and #20457a-#2f609b (F-GSQR_2).

Sunset sky and cloud deck. The horizon band is desaturated (#d7c3a2 against #facc6c and #ffc9bd). The cloud deck below the horizon is light beige (#c4b2a6, and #d3b8a6 in q21). Real sunset photos show a dark violet or blue-grey deck (#8a68a5/#7b5d99, #2d3238).
Wing at sunset. The upper wing is warm brown (#816358-#896b61). The photos show it cool mauve-violet from sky reflection (#7e73b8), or as a dark neutral silhouette (#4f4a4e).
Night sky. Stars, a dark cloud deck and a faint wing silhouette. Plausible, but there is no in-flight reference for this cabin.
Nav lights and strobe at the raked tip. Present, with the red on the left, and visible in the studio tip view.

issues.detail: The 777-300ER wing carries a wide black chordwise stripe on the upper surface at the outer main-wheel line. It is the tail-camera taxi reference, and ANA's 777s add a yellow ice-detection spot on it. It is the most conspicuous marking in any over-wing cabin view (19A/q12 at z 36.4 looks straight at it). The model has none.
issues.problem: Missing gear-alignment stripe and ANA yellow ice spot on the upper wing
issues.evidence: ref/web/wing/Cabin_wing_view_of_Air_France_777_F-GSQR_1.jpg and _2.jpg (777-328ER cruise window views): a black band about 0.35 m wide runs fore-aft across the wing ahead of the spoilers. ref/web/exterior/agn_Boeing-777-wing-stripes-1-1024x700.jpeg (overhead 777-300ER): at 34.7 px/m from the 6.2 m fuselage, the stripe centre is about 6.4 m from the centreline, about 0.4 m wide, and runs from about 1 m ahead of the flap trailing edge about 5.6 m forward. Sources: aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/why-boeing-777-black-stripes-wings ('aligned with the outboard edge of the main landing gear'), supercarblondie.com/every-boeing-777-has-these-black-stripes-on-its-wings. airlinercafe.com/forums/topic/yellow-areas-on-ana-wing says 'ANA's 777s have a large stripe with a yellow spot'.
issues.fix: In buildExterior, after the spoiler lines, add wingLine(B, side, [[6.4, 33.2],[6.4, 36.0],[6.4, 38.8]], {c:'#15171a', r:0.9, m:0}, 0.38). A 0.38 m-wide strip along nose stations 33.2-38.8 at s = 6.4 m; lift it 0.014 m so it clears the seam strips it crosses. Add the ANA yellow ice spot as a second wingLine at [[6.4, 35.2],[6.4, 35.8]], width 0.30, colour '#e8c21e'. Its size and position are unknown (see questions), so leave it out until confirmed.

issues.detail: The flap-track fairing loft uses a depth floor of 0.35 and a width floor of 0.55 (depth 0.85 × 0.35 + 0.04 = 0.34 m at the tail), so each canoe tapers to a thin spike ending in a small nub. From the aft PY/Y windows (26A, 30A) they read as flat dark paddles.
issues.problem: Canoe tails too thin and pointed
issues.evidence: ref/web/wing/Boeing_777_(4139974954)_(2).jpg: the canoe aft of the flap stays deep and slab-sided, and its rounded end is roughly 70 % of the maximum depth. Compare scratchpad/qa/ext/st/w_under.png and ext/f_30A.png, where the tails are spikes.
issues.fix: In the canoe loop of buildExterior, change the tail law to Math.max(0.75, Math.pow(c, 0.3)) for depth and Math.max(0.8, Math.pow(c, 0.25)) for width. Scale the rounded-end quarter-ellipse to 0.8*e (width) and 0.72*e (depth) instead of 0.55*e / 0.35*e, and raise RE from 0.32 to 0.40 m so the end is a blunt dome about 0.65 m tall.

issues.detail: From the window, the sunset cloud deck and horizon read as a light beige wash. The photos show a narrow saturated orange band over a dark violet/blue-grey deck, with a blue-violet sky above.
issues.problem: Sunset deck far too bright and warm, horizon band desaturated
issues.evidence: ref/web/wing/yt/p97zMaCMWRg.jpg (777 GE90 window view at sunset): deck #8a68a5/#7b5d99, horizon #ffc9bd, sky +15° #8e9dee. ref/web/exterior/Air_France_Boeing_777-300ER_Greenland_Sunrise_2022.jpg (777-300ER): deck #2d3238, horizon #facc6c, sky #718083. Model s_15A: deck #c4b2a6, horizon #d7c3a2, pane top #b69eac. q21 deck #d3b8a6.
issues.fix: src/12_scene.js SKIES.sunset: set cloudLit to [0.70, 0.46, 0.52] and cloudShade to [0.20, 0.17, 0.30] (deck target about #7a6090 at the window). Set horizon to [1.35, 0.62, 0.22] and haze to [0.55, 0.36, 0.42], and keep the horizon band within about 3° so it renders about #f5c070. Set zenith to [0.14, 0.20, 0.62] so +15° renders about #8a96d8.

issues.detail: At |x| = 2.6 (winExp = 1) the day sky in the pane is pale grey-blue from the top of the window down to the horizon. Cruise photos from 777 windows show a saturated blue gradient with a thin white haze only at the horizon.
issues.problem: Day sky too washed out at the window
issues.evidence: ref/web/wing/Cabin_wing_view_of_Air_France_777_F-GSQR_1.jpg: #4d7098 at +20° down to #9bb1c6 just above the horizon. F-GSQR_2: #20457a-#2f609b-#93c3f3. ref/web/exterior/Air_France_Boeing_777-300ER_Greenland_2022.jpg: #206cc4 zenith. Model f_19A/f_17A: #abc2d8 at the top of the pane, #bccbda at the horizon.
issues.fix: SKIES.day: set horizon to [0.42, 0.60, 0.90] and haze to [0.80, 0.86, 0.94], and confine the haze to the lowest ~4° of elevation (steeper exponent in the sky shader's horizon blend). Target about #5578a8 at +15° and #a8bfd6 at +3° when rendered at winExp 1. Leave winExp at 1.6 for the away-from-window view.

issues.detail: The wing crest is linear (crest(s) = -0.02 + (s-4)*0.0915, the ground dihedral), so the outer wing looks ruler-straight from the cabin. In cruise the 777 wing bends up, and both window photos show the leading edge and far wing edge curving upward toward the raked tip.
issues.evidence: ref/web/wing/Cabin_wing_view_of_Air_France_777_F-GSQR_1.jpg and F-GSQR_2.jpg: the leading edge projects as a concave-up curve rising to the tip, which a straight 3-D edge cannot do. Compare scratchpad/qa/ext/f_17A.png and st/b_front.png, where both are straight.
issues.fix: In WING.crest add a quadratic flight-bending term: crest: (s) => -0.02 + (s - 4) * 0.0915 + 1.5 * Math.pow(Math.max(0, s - 4) / 28.4, 2). This gives about +1.5 m at the tip; the magnitude is [A], so tune it by overlaying a 17A render on F-GSQR_2. Move the nav and strobe lights with it; they already follow stations. Keep the nacelle and pylon at their current positions, since the inboard term is under 0.05 m at s = 9.6.

issues.detail: From 13A the pylon shows as a flat 0.16 m slab along the cowl crest. It renders #3e4b62, darker and bluer than both the cowl (#c9d2dc) and the lit wing (#aeb4b9). The same pylon renders #a1a1a4 in the studio (st/w_eng.png), so in the cabin view the faces the viewer sees are lit by sky only, or their normals are inverted.
issues.problem: Pylon reads as a dark blue plank on top of the nacelle
issues.evidence: ref/web/wing/(GBR-London)_All_Nippon_Airways_Boeing_777-300ER_JA797A_@_EGLL_2025-06-17.jpg crop: the pylon and strut above the nacelle are light grey, the same as the wing. ref/web/wing/yt/p97zMaCMWRg.jpg: the pylon rises as a distinct swept ridge. Model: scratchpad/qa/ext/f_13A.png (500,296) = #3e4b62.
issues.fix: In the pylon loop of buildExterior, raise the forward part: top = nacTop(x) + lerp(0.10, 0.45, smooth(1.6, leE - E.x0, x)) instead of +0.04, so a sloping ridge meets the leading edge. Paint it paint (#636466) rather than paintLow. Check that gLoft under M4.trs(0,0,0,0,π/2) keeps outward normals; the canoe and pylon lofts should use the same fixWinding path as wingLine.

issues.detail: At sunset the upper wing renders warm brown (#816358-#896b61). The photos show a low-sun wing surface dominated by sky reflection: cool mauve-violet, or a dark neutral silhouette.
issues.problem: Wing colour at sunset too orange-brown
issues.evidence: ref/web/wing/yt/p97zMaCMWRg.jpg: upper wing #7e73b8, underside #342c5f. ref/web/exterior/Air_France_Boeing_777-300ER_Greenland_Sunrise_2022.jpg: wing #4f4a4e-#6f4f50. Model: scratchpad/qa/ext/s_19A_fwd.png (100,300) = #896b61.
issues.fix: SKIES.sunset: lower the sun colour to [3.0, 1.5, 0.6] so grazing direct light weakens, and raise the exterior sky-reflection/ambient from skyTop [0.45,0.35,0.45] to [0.40,0.36,0.62]. Target an upper wing of about #6e6488 at 5° sun elevation.

questionsForUser: ANA's 777s reportedly have a yellow ice-detection spot on the black gear-alignment stripe (airlinercafe forum). Do you have an ANA 777-300ER over-wing photo showing its size and position? Without one I would add the black stripe only.

Does the ANA 777-300ER wing carry the dotted overwing escape-route/walkway outline next to the fuselage (visible on other 777s in overhead photos, e.g. agn_Boeing-777-wing-stripes)? Should it be modelled, given it may be hidden by the fuselage curvature from most windows?
Is there a GE90 logo on the ANA fan cowls? The JA797A photo shows a small mark on the lower aft cowl at low resolution, but the model notes say no titles.
How much in-flight wing bending do you want? About +1.5 m at the tip is my estimate from the F-GSQR photos; no published 777-300ER cruise deflection figure was found.
